mappings.note: Defective row: the stem asks why Maxwell went to Basra while the options and key are about Mij tearing the lining of the box. Either question is answered from a stated fact, so LO-1.
The rubber ball Mij shuffled round the room is named in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
Southern Iraq is stated in the opening; retrieval, LO-1.
Camusfearna's setting by water is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The Tigris marshes are named in the friend's remark; retrieval, LO-1.
Basra is stated as their destination; retrieval, LO-1.
The religious holiday that closed the exchange is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The coating of mud is described in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
Chocolate-brown fur is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The month it took for the true colour to show is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
That zoologists gave the species its Latin name is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Mij coming onto the bed after midnight is narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
'Elaborate' on Mij's playfulness requires the learner to assemble the incidents that show it - textual evidence, LO-3.

Keeping a pet as a life of commitment, worked through what Maxwell actually did for Mij on the journey. That is LO-9 - the duty of care illustrated from the narrator's conduct - rather than LO-8's question of whether an otter should be a pet.
Judges from Mij's own behaviour whether an otter can live in a city flat - evaluating a wild animal's fitness for pet life, LO-8.
Mij's love of water is stated in the bathroom passage; retrieval, LO-1.
'Give an example from the text' is an explicit evidence requirement, LO-3.
The scene on the plane is narrated in full; retrieval, LO-1.
Supplies the right partitive for each noun (a lump of clay, a cloud of smoke). Collocation and word meaning, C-E1.1.
A dumb-charades activity in which feelings are expressed and guessed. Expression, C-E1.2; nothing is retrieved from the text.
Write your own description of a person or pet you love. Composition with attention to detail and feeling, C-E1.2.
The daily wall-galloping routine is narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
Mij's first aloofness and then his approach to the bed are both narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
Retell the flight in the air hostess's voice. A first-person narrative in an assigned role, C-E1.2.
The London month - games, walks, the primary-school wall - is narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
Both halves are stated: the mail at the Consulate-General and the sack the Arabs brought. Retrieval, LO-1.
Asks why Mij was aloof at first and which explanation for his coming to the bed does NOT hold - inference about the animal's state, LO-2, not a lifted fact.
Tests a quoted claim about water against what Mij actually did, so the answer must cite the text - LO-3. It is not LO-8, which is about fitness for pet life.
How Mij passed his time in play is described in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
'Justify the statement with examples from the text' is the evidence outcome, LO-3.
His reason for wanting an otter and how he came by one are both narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
Parts sort statements into fact and opinion and gloss 'groping' (C-E1.1); the final 40-word part asks for examples of Mij's resourcefulness from the text (LO-3).
Asks why the author sets Mij's rituals beside schoolchildren's - the writer's purpose in drawing the comparison, LO-2.
Two parts are synonym questions for 'booked' and 'out of order' (C-E1.1); the last asks what the five-day wait shows about communication in that period, an inference about context (LO-2).
Authorship of 'Mijbil the Otter'. Knowledge about the work, C-E1.4.
Fill-in of the destination from the opening sentence; retrieval, LO-1.
Camusfearna is named as his home; retrieval, LO-1.
The 'experiment' of keeping an otter at Camusfearna is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Five days is a stated figure; retrieval, LO-1.
The two Arabs who delivered the sack are named in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
